record.context_brief: When the minimal-distance set is an interval
record.original_question: Does there exist a finite abelian group G for which the set Delta*(G) = {min Delta(G0) : G0 subset G and Delta(G0) is nonempty} is an interval and, at the same time, the exponent of G is at least 2r(G) + 2, where r(G) is the rank of G?

evidence.quote: For |G| > 1, there are uniquely determined integers 1 < n1 | ... | nr such that G ~= C_{n1} ⊕ ... ⊕ C_{nr}. We denote by r(G) = r the rank of G and by exp(G) = nr the exponent of G.
For |G| >= 3, one denotes by Delta*(G) = {min Delta(G0) : G0 subset G, Delta(G0) != empty}.
Problem 6.21. Is there a finite abelian group G such that Delta*(G) is an interval and exp(G) >= 2r(G) + 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|>1$. Then there exist uniquely determined integers $1<n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ such that 
$$G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus C_{n_2}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r},$$
where $C_n$ denotes the cyclic group of order $n$. Define the rank of $G$ by $\mathsf r(G)=r$ and the exponent of $G$ by $\exp(G)=n_r$.

For a subset $G_0\subseteq G$, let $\mathcal F(G_0)$ denote the free abelian monoid on $G_0$ (whose elements are formal multisets, called sequences, over $G_0$). For $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_\ell\in\mathcal F(G_0)$, let $\sigma(S)=g_1+\cdots+g_\ell\in G$. The sequence $S$ is called a zero-sum sequence if $\sigma(S)=0$, and a minimal zero-sum sequence if $\sigma(S)=0$ and no proper nonempty subsequence has sum zero. For a zero-sum sequence $S$, a factorization of $S$ is an unordered decomposition of $S$ into minimal zero-sum sequences, and the length of such a factorization is the number of minimal zero-sum factors. The set of lengths $\mathsf L(S)$ is the set of all possible factorization lengths of $S$. For a subset $G_0\subseteq G$, define
$$\Delta(G_0)=\bigcup_{S}\{\,\ell_{i+1}-\ell_i : \mathsf L(S)=\{\ell_1<\ell_2<\cdots\}\,\},$$
the union being taken over all zero-sum sequences $S$ over $G_0$ (the set of successive differences appearing in length sets).

Define
$$\Delta^*(G)=\{\min\Delta(G_0) : G_0\subseteq G\text{ and }\Delta(G_0)\neq\varnothing\}\subseteq\mathbb N.$$

Question: Does there exist a finite abelian group $G$ such that $\Delta^*(G)$ is an interval of $\mathbb N$ (i.e., a set of consecutive positive integers) and at the same time
$$\exp(G)\;\geq\;2\,\mathsf r(G)+2\;?$$
artifact.category_tag: Non-unique factorization in finite abelian groups
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution to the question of whether there exists a finite abelian group with $\Delta^*(G)$ an interval and $\exp(G)\geq 2\mathsf r(G)+2$. Subsequent literature on $\Delta^*(G)$ by Geroldinger, Schmid, and others continues to investigate the structure of $\Delta^*(G)$, but no source found in this search states that this particular question has been settled.

status_evidence.title: On minimal distances in Krull monoids with infinite class group
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Δ*(G) and minimal distances in factorization theory but does not resolve the specific intersection of conditions on intervals and exp(G) ≥ 2 r(G)+2.
status_evidence.claim: Related work continues but does not state a resolution of the specific problem.
